classification: Authorized read-only metadata diagnostic, performed by implementation agent. Separate caller from signed Final production helper.

commands.command: Run the owned diagnostic once with subprocess timeout=10, stderr discarded, stdout parsed and allowed JSON fields checked before saving

interpretation: At the sampled time, both WindowServer and ScreenCaptureKit omit Safari from onscreen windows while agreeing on the offscreen set. The current picker onScreenWindowsOnly:true excludes that set. Safari non-regular/hidden state is not the observed cause.
privacy: Only Safari PID/state, windowID/layer/onScreen/rect and diagnostic status/time were serialized. No title/URL/AX tree/image, other-app window metadata, raw system error text or runtime stderr was saved. Enumeration APIs supply system objects internally; sensitive fields were never read into the output.
noMutations: No AX action, mouse or key input
limits: Different executable/caller and a later sample than the failed picker, so not an exact in-process reproduction.
No proof that these windowIDs are the previously attempted private window; root can correlate separately.
Offscreen metadata does not distinguish another Space, minimized/fullscreen window or other WindowServer reason.
Screen permission was already true. False-preflight exit path was source-reviewed, not executed against an unpermitted caller.
This does not establish real Safari background navigation support.
